newsitem.title: ITALY: Greenpeace founder pays tribute to Cousteau.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace founder pays tribute to Cousteau.

text.p: The founder of environmental group Greenpeace International paid tribute to Jacques-Yves Cousteau on Wednesday, saying the French sea explorer had dedicated his life to saving the world's oceans.

"Whenever we needed help in our fight for the environment, Cousteau was always available," David McTaggart said in a statement from his home in Italy shortly after Cousteau's death on Wednesday morning. He was 87.
"The threats to the oceans that Cousteau loved and worked so hard to protect throughout his lifetime are increasingly serious and require more urgent action than ever to counteract," McTaggart said.
"As he often reminded us, all hands are needed to safeguard the seas that sustain us and all life on Earth."
McTaggart said Cousteau had often helped Greenpeace in its campaigns to protect marine areas, including protests against French nuclear testing on Muroroa atoll in the South Pacific.

He said the French oceanographer, who was best known for his prize-winning films of the underwater world, had also helped to secure international support for an agreement to protect the Antarctic from commercial mining.
